🇲🇽🌎 <u>"Shield of the Americas": 17 Countries Signed Up. Mexico Isn't One of Them</u>

Seventeen governments, from Argentina and Bolivia to Panama, Peru and Trinidad and Tobago, have joined Trump and Rubio's "Shield of the Americas", which is sold as a fight against "narcoterrorism". Mexico isn't on the list. In March, Sheinbaum said Mexico didn't need an invitation because it already has its own agreement with Washington. In Contralínea, Marcela Román Valadez describes what Mexico already lived through as the "war on drugs": "the authorized deployment of US military operations to intervene in internal affairs."
banner: SHIELD OF THE AMERICAS: 17 IN, MEXICO OUT

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Magistrate Charged With Rape Is Suspended Again</u>

Mexico's Federal Administrative Justice Tribunal (TFJA) suspended magistrate Pedro Rodríguez Chandoquí again on September 25, after reinstating him on August 4. The reinstatement had consequences: the criminal judge who indicted him for aggravated rape cited his tribunal job as proof he was "rooted" in Mexico City and let him go free pending trial. The tribunal reversed course after Contralínea raised the case at the presidential press conference. The Women's Ministry, headed by Laura Itzel Castillo, called for a gender-perspective investigation: "No public office can be an advantage over a victim."

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>From Gaza to La Condesa: Mexico's Palestinian Refugees</u>

Mohamed Abed, a 36-year-old Palestinian systems engineer, reached Mexico in 2025 with 17 relatives, after Israeli bombing in Gaza killed his four-year-old daughter. Before dawn on Tuesdays he now loads his motorized tricycle with Palestinian food to sell at an open-air market in La Condesa. He is one of about 160 Palestinians living in Mexico, and half of them have refugee status. His son Yusuf was born here in May: "He was born in Mexico, but he carries Gaza's roots in his heart."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>500 US Troops on the Border? Mexico Answers From Its Own Side</u>

Mexico's Navy (Semar) and Foreign Ministry (SRE) say the 500 US soldiers deployed to Texas' Rio Grande Valley are part of "mirror operations": each country acts in parallel, and only inside its own territory. Washington calls its deployment "Vanguardia Ardiente". Mexico answered from Matamoros under Operación Sable with 159 marines, 11 vehicles and two drones, all on Mexican soil.

🇲🇽📈 <u>IMF: Mexico grows 1.5% in 2026 and 1.8% in 2027</u>

In its 2026 Article IV review of Mexico, the International Monetary Fund projects 1.5% GDP growth this year and 1.8% in 2027, as El Financiero reports. Foreign trade is the main driver. That is above the 1.4% that private analysts forecast in Banxico's latest survey.

The Fund noted progress on fiscal consolidation and a lower deficit. It still wants Mexico to cut its debt faster, even though Mexico already has one of the lowest debt-to-GDP ratios in the OECD.

🇲🇽📊 <u>Two years in, Sheinbaum stands at 70% approval</u>

El Financiero's national poll puts President Claudia Sheinbaum at 70% approval as she completes her second year. That is up two points from last month and her highest level since March. Disapproval is 30%.

The poll interviewed 800 adults by phone between September 10 and 20. Respondents also rated social programs, security and the fight against corruption better than a year earlier. Those two years included tariff threats, pressure from Rubio and a steady campaign against her in the press.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Dos Bocas "fire": Olmeca refinery running normally</u>

Early Thursday, posts spread claiming that the Olmeca refinery was on fire. Pemex says the fire was in dry grass around the flare of the Litoral Separation Battery at the Dos Bocas Maritime Terminal, outside the refinery.

Overnight, gas had been diverted to the flare so that producing wells in the Southwest Marine Region would not have to be shut in. The heat set the dry grass alight, and terminal firefighters put it out. Pemex reported no injuries, no damage to facilities, and the refinery running as normal.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>FGR: "conclusive evidence" against PAN ex-governor Ruffo</u>

Ernesto Ruffo Appel became Mexico's first opposition governor in 1989, when the PAN took Baja California. The Fiscalía General de la República (FGR) says it has "datos de prueba contundentes" that he took part in running Ingemar. Prosecutors call it the largest tax-fuel smuggling network ever detected in Mexico: it declared only 10% of the fuel it imported from the US.

According to the FGR, Ruffo admitted owning 49% of the company. Prosecutors say he knew since at least 2024 that tankers carrying 30,000, 40,000, 110,000 and 112,000 liters were being declared as 10,000-liter loads. He is now under house arrest, and the case continues.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>US seizes Cuba-bound fuel ship and escorts it to Mexico's Progreso</u>

The US Coast Guard boarded the cargo ship Grace in the Caribbean, between Cuba and Mexico, on September 5. Washington only disclosed it on October 2. The 91-meter vessel was escorted to the Yucatán port of Progreso, where the Mexican Navy inspected it and found fuel stored in its ballast tanks. Washington calls it "coordinated actions" by both governments.

It's the second fuel shipment to Cuba intercepted in a matter of weeks. Fuel for an island already living under a 60-year blockade is now treated as contraband on the high seas.
banner: CUBA FUEL SHIP SEIZED, TOWED TO PROGRESO

🇲🇽🏭 <u>Car Sales: Best January–September on Record</u>

INEGI: Mexico sold 129,288 new light vehicles in September, up 8.0% year on year and the seventh straight month of growth. From January to September the total is 1,144,002 units, up 5.0%, beating 2016's record pace by 21,860 vehicles (via El Economista).
